reasoning: Dynamic programming over consumed digits keeps every attainable prefix gcd, with a bitset of attainable segment counts for that gcd. Append each next segment of at most M digits, updating gcd and shifting the count bitset. Prune only counts that cannot meet the final separator bounds even with minimum/maximum remaining segment lengths. Leading zeroes and gcd(0,0)=0 are handled by ordinary integer accumulation. Keeping all gcd states avoids the invalid greedy assumption that the largest intermediate gcd always leads to the best final result.
